title: EchoNext ECG flag finds severe aortic stenosis in an asymptomatic 84-year-old; TAVR after hip-fracture surgery
summary: At Columbia/NewYork-Presbyterian, EchoNext flagged a pre-operative ECG (score 0.6094), triggering an EHR advisory; echo showed LVEF 40% and severe aortic stenosis; cardiac anesthesia, surgery, TAVR.
account: Tat et al. (JACC: Case Reports, 4 March 2026) describe an 84-year-old woman with hypertension admitted after a fall with a left femur fracture. Her ECG was analyzed by EchoNext, a deep-learning model for structural heart disease developed at Columbia; the earlier verifier recorded a score of 0.6094 (the model's high-risk cutoff is 0.6), which triggered an electronic-health-record advisory. Transthoracic echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 40% and severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.6 cm2, peak velocity 3.9 m/s, mean gradient 34 mm Hg); cardiology recommended cardiac anesthesia for the orthopedic operation, and the patient then underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement (on day 8 per the earlier reason). The authors call it the first report of an AI-ECG algorithm detecting undiagnosed severe aortic stenosis that led to TAVR. EchoNext's development paper (Poterucha et al., Nature, July 2025) reports training on more than 1 million ECG and imaging records and that 73% of patients flagged high-risk in prospective evaluation had newly diagnosed disease. All authors are the Columbia developers; Dr Elias reports research support including from Edwards. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Screen ECGs for unrecognised structural heart disease and alert clinicians through the electronic health record
system: EchoNext deep-learning ECG model integrated into the electronic health record
deployer: Columbia University Irving Medical Center / NewYork-Presbyterian
segment: Hospital patients with an ECG and no known structural heart disease
taxonomy_note: Developer-authored case report (academic in-house model); no non-developer account of the case exists, which is why the earlier verifier set it aside while calling it a strong candidate. The 0.6094 score and day-8 TAVR come from the earlier reason; the fetched text gives the 0.6 cutoff and the echo findings.
